input.content:
RESOLVED, and the prescription in this item was wrong about the obstacle -- worth recording because that is the transferable part.

LANDED: Ledger/P1Vanishing.lean (AJC), 0 sorries, kernel EXIT=0.
 * LaurentChartData.subsingleton_h1Cok -- Cech H1(O) = 0 on the two-chart cover of ANY Spec k-scheme carrying Laurent chart data. No properness, smoothness, irreducibility, cohomological finiteness; the section binds only [Field k] and Y.
 * subsingleton_hModule_one_p1Over, genus_p1Over_eq_zero -- on the genus carrier at P1, every field.
 * uniformBaseDivisor_p1Over, uniformVanishing_p1Over -- r7's producers with the antecedent supplied, so extension-uniform bounded vanishing is now WITNESSED at a curve AJC has (threshold 0), not merely implied.

WHERE THIS ITEM WAS WRONG. It said the real obstacle is structural: LaurentChartData carries span_pow_x and span_pow_y (each CHART ring is the k-span of nonneg powers) but no field saying the OVERLAP is spanned by INTEGER powers; that adding a field "breaks every LaurentChartData constructor in the project"; and that deriving it instead "needs the basic-open localization Gamma(V0 cap V1) = Gamma(V0)[x^-1] plus a span-of-localization lemma", recommended as a standalone next to module_finite_H1Cok.

None of that was needed. LaurentChartData.span_ladder_overlap derives the overlap span from the fields ALREADY THERE, in about 20 lines, using three lemmas already in Adelic/FinitenessP1.lean:
 * exists_pow_mul_eq_res IS the basic-open localization this item asked someone to build. It already packages IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_of_eq_basicOpen + IsLocalization.surj, and it is consumed twice by module_finite_H1Cok in the same file.
 * span_ladder_of_pow_mul_mem_span converts "t^n * m lies in the nonneg-power span for some n" into "the two-sided ladder spans", from t*u = 1 -- exactly the shape exists_pow_mul_eq_res produces.
 * the chart span transports along the restriction Gamma(V0) -> Gamma(V0 cap V1) because that restriction is a k-algebra map (toModuleKSheaf.algebraMap_naturality). That step is the smul case of exists_finset_forall_mem_span_pow_mul with module-finiteness dropped; extracted here as mem_span_pow_map_of_span_pow.

So the item's own recommendation ("derive rather than add a field", "next to module_finite_H1Cok, the natural neighbour") pointed at the right file and the right neighbour, and then over-priced what remained by naming a brick that was already sitting in it.

ALSO LANDED, separately: sup_eq_top_of_laurent_pair_span_one, the surjectivity counterpart of module_finite_quotient_of_laurent_pair. Same Laurent-pair data; with the generator set {1} the two lattices do not merely have finite-dimensional quotient, they exhaust M. Pure algebra, reusable.

GENERALISATION, since this lane has now mis-priced in both directions: before extending a bundled structure, check whether the thing you are about to add is already a CONSEQUENCE of its existing fields, and whether a sibling theorem in that same file already consumes them the way you need. A prescription in a handoff is the least-tested claim in it -- it was written by whoever stopped BECAUSE of it, so nothing downstream has ever re-derived it.

SCOPE UNCHANGED where it should be. Genus 0 only. Extension-uniformity for genus >= 1 keeps r7's exact residue: UniformBaseDivisor C d for d > 0, needing a divisor-level base-change comparison AJC does not have. Global generation untouched by this file.
